newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai bourse denies intervening in big lot trades.
newsitem.headline: Thai bourse denies intervening in big lot trades.

text.p: The Stock Market of Thailand on Tuesday denied that the authorities had asked local brokerages not to handle big lot stocks transactions with foreigners.
The SET's executive vice president Surat Palalikit said all trading at the exchange was continuing as normal.

He made the statement in response to a Reuters report quoting brokers as saying that they had been informally told by the Bank of Thailand not to handle big lots. "There had been absolutely no attempt to interfere in big lot trading on the alien board, or any other market activity," he said in a statement.

Brokers earlier said the central bank's informal directive to brokers was aimed at stopping offshore foreign exchange speculators, in urgent need of baht, to raise the currency through stocks sales on the bourse.
Stock exchange officials, when contacted on the brokers comments earlier on Tuesday, told Reuters they had not heard of any such move.
Surat said foreign investors were entitled to remit proceeds from their trading activities according to central bank regulations.
The Securities and Exchange Commission, which regulates the bourse, said on Tuesday that the central bank would require foreigners dealing in Thai stocks to settle in U.S. dollars only temporarily.
The measure would apply to the foreign board only, a senior SEC official said.
Separately, the central bank said it would ask institutions providing custodian services not to transfer unpaid stocks to foreign accounts.
Brokers said the move could help slow selling of Thai stocks by foreign investors who had resorted to short sales of stocks to raise funds in baht.
